questions.question_text: Which of the following errors will not affect the agreement of a Trial Balance?
options: A) Error of undercasting a subsidiary book
C) Posting an entry to the wrong side of an account
questions.answer: B) Error of complete omission

questions.question_text: A Trial Balance is a statement prepared to check the:
options: A) Arithmetical accuracy of ledger accounts
B) Financial position of the business
questions.answer: A) Arithmetical accuracy of ledger accounts

questions.question_text: If a suspense account is opened to tally the trial balance, its balance is carried forward to the next year if:
options: A) It represents personal or real accounts
D) The accountant decides to close it to Capital
questions.answer: A) It represents personal or real accounts

questions.question_text: Under the written down value method, depreciation is calculated on:
options: A) The original cost of the asset
B) The market value of the asset
C) The book value of the asset at the beginning of the year
D) The scrap value of the asset
questions.answer: C) The book value of the asset at the beginning of the year

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a cause of depreciation?
questions.answer: C) Fluctuation in market price

questions.question_text: A Provision is created out of:
questions.answer: B) Current year's profits

questions.question_text: Which reserve is created to meet an unknown liability?
questions.answer: B) General Reserve

questions.question_text: Wages paid for the installation of a new machinery should be debited to:
questions.answer: B) Machinery Account

questions.question_text: Gross Profit is equal to:
options: A) Net Sales - Cost of Goods Sold
D) Net Sales - Direct Expenses only
questions.answer: A) Net Sales - Cost of Goods Sold

questions.question_text: Closing stock is valued at:
options: C) Cost price or Net Realizable Value, whichever is lower
D) Cost price or Net Realizable Value, whichever is higher
questions.answer: C) Cost price or Net Realizable Value, whichever is lower

questions.question_text: Outstanding wages are shown as a:
questions.answer: C) Current Liability

questions.question_text: Income received in advance is a:
questions.answer: A) Liability

questions.question_text: The purpose of preparing a Trading Account is to ascertain:
options: A) Net Profit or Net Loss
C) Gross Profit or Gross Loss
questions.answer: C) Gross Profit or Gross Loss

questions.question_text: Marshalling of Balance Sheet refers to:
options: A) Auditing the assets and liabilities
B) Arranging assets and liabilities in a specific order
questions.answer: B) Arranging assets and liabilities in a specific order

questions.question_text: Under incomplete records, profit is ascertained by comparing:
options: A) Opening capital and opening assets
B) Opening capital and closing capital
C) Total assets and total liabilities
questions.answer: B) Opening capital and closing capital

questions.question_text: A statement of affairs is similar to a:
questions.answer: C) Balance Sheet

questions.question_text: Goodwill is classified as an:
questions.answer: B) Intangible fixed asset

questions.question_text: If closing stock is given inside the trial balance, it is shown in:
options: C) Both Trading Account and Balance Sheet
questions.answer: B) Balance Sheet only

questions.question_text: Accrued income is recognized based on which accounting concept?
questions.answer: B) Accrual concept

questions.question_text: Which error is committed when a transaction is recorded with the wrong amount in the book of original entry?
questions.answer: B) Error of commission

questions.question_text: Distinguish between an Error of Principle and an Error of Omission. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: An error of principle occurs when accounting principles are violated, like treating capital expenditure as revenue. An error of omission happens when a transaction is partially or completely unrecorded in the books.

questions.question_text: State the primary difference between a Provision and a Reserve. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A provision is a charge against profit created for a known liability of uncertain amount. A reserve is an appropriation of profit created to strengthen the business's overall financial position.

questions.question_text: Why is depreciation charged on fixed assets? Give two main reasons. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Depreciation is charged to ascertain the true net profit by matching expenses against revenues, and to present the true and fair financial position by showing assets at their realistic book value.

questions.question_text: Define Operating Profit in the context of financial statements. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Operating profit is the profit earned from the normal core activities of a business. It is calculated by deducting operating expenses from gross profit, excluding non-operating incomes and non-operating expenses.

questions.question_text: Explain the treatment of 'Prepaid Insurance' given in the adjustments outside the Trial Balance. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Prepaid insurance must be deducted from the insurance expense on the debit side of the Profit & Loss Account and simultaneously shown on the asset side of the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: What is a Statement of Affairs in the context of incomplete records? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A statement of affairs is a statement of assets and liabilities prepared under the single entry system to estimate the capital of a business at a specific point in time.

questions.question_text: Rectify the following errors: (i) Credit sales to Mohan $5,000 were not recorded. (ii) Machinery purchased for $10,000 was debited to Purchases Account. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: For (i): Debit Mohan A/c $5,000 and Credit Sales A/c $5,000 to record the omitted sale. For (ii): Debit Machinery A/c $10,000 and Credit Purchases A/c $10,000 to correct the error of principle.

questions.question_text: A Trial Balance shows a difference of $400 on the debit side, placed in a Suspense Account. Later, it was found that goods purchased for $400 were correctly entered in the Cash Book but not posted to the Purchases Account. Pass the rectifying entry. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The Purchases Account was undercast by $400. To rectify, Debit Purchases Account with $400 and Credit Suspense Account with $400. This clears the suspense account balance and corrects the partial omission.

questions.question_text: Calculate the Cost of Goods Sold from the following: Opening Stock $15,000, Purchases $40,000, Direct Wages $5,000, Closing Stock $10,000. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Cost of Goods Sold = Opening Stock ($15,000) + Purchases ($40,000) + Direct Wages ($5,000) - Closing Stock ($10,000). The Cost of Goods Sold evaluates to $50,000.

questions.question_text: A machine was purchased on April 1, 2024, for $50,000. Depreciation is charged at 10% p.a. using the Straight Line Method. Calculate the book value of the machine on March 31, 2026. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Annual depreciation is 10% of $50,000 = $5,000. For two years (2024-25 and 2025-26), total depreciation is $10,000. The book value on March 31, 2026, is original cost ($50,000) minus accumulated depreciation ($10,000) = $40,000.

questions.question_text: Explain the concept of grouping and marshalling in a Balance Sheet. Give the order of liquidity. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Grouping means putting similar items under a common heading. Marshalling is arranging them in a specific order. Under the order of liquidity, assets are arranged from most liquid (Cash) to least liquid (Goodwill), and liabilities from short-term to long-term.

questions.question_text: Provide the adjusting journal entry for Manager’s Commission of 5% on net profit before charging such commission, assuming the net profit before commission is $21,000. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Manager's commission = 5% of $21,000 = $1,050. The entry is: Debit Profit & Loss Account $1,050; Credit Manager's Commission Outstanding Account $1,050. This records the expense and creates the liability.

questions.question_text: Rahul keeps incomplete records. His opening capital is $40,000 and closing capital is $55,000. During the year, he introduced $10,000 as fresh capital and withdrew $5,000 for personal use. Calculate his profit or loss. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Profit = Closing Capital ($55,000) + Drawings ($5,000) - Additional Capital ($10,000) - Opening Capital ($40,000). Calculation: $60,000 - $50,000 = $10,000. Rahul made a Net Profit of $10,000 during the year.

questions.question_text: How will you treat 'Interest on Capital' and 'Interest on Drawings' while preparing final accounts? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Interest on Capital is debited to P&L A/c and added to Capital in the Balance Sheet. Interest on Drawings is credited to P&L A/c and deducted from Capital (or added to drawings) in the Balance Sheet.

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer (LA) / Problem Solving

questions.question_text: The Trial Balance of Mr. X failed to agree and the difference was placed in a Suspense Account. Rectify the following errors and prepare the Suspense Account: 1. Sales book overcast by $1,000. 2. $500 paid for repairs to building was debited to Building Account. 3. Goods returned by Shyam $400 were not posted to his account. 4. Purchase of furniture for $2,000 was entered in the Purchases book. [80-100 words]
questions.answer: Entries: 1) Debit Sales A/c $1,000, Credit Suspense A/c $1,000. 2) Debit Repairs A/c $500, Credit Building A/c $500 (No Suspense). 3) Debit Suspense A/c $400, Credit Shyam's A/c $400. 4) Debit Furniture A/c $2,000, Credit Purchases A/c $2,000 (No Suspense). In the Suspense Account layout: The credit side has 'By Sales A/c $1,000'. The debit side has 'To Shyam's A/c $400'. The balancing figure is an opening debit balance of $600 ('To Difference in Trial Balance $600') to close the account.

questions.question_text: A firm purchased a plant for $100,000 on April 1, 2023. It charges depreciation at 20% p.a. on the Written Down Value method. On October 1, 2025, a part of the plant costing $20,000 on April 1, 2023, became obsolete and was sold for $8,000. Detail the calculations for the profit or loss on the sale of this specific machine part. [70-90 words]
questions.answer: Original cost of the sold part on April 1, 2023: $20,000. Depreciation for 2023-24 (20%): $4,000. WDV on April 1, 2024: $16,000. Depreciation for 2024-25 (20%): $3,200. WDV on April 1, 2025: $12,800. Depreciation for 6 months until Oct 1, 2025 (20% for half year): $1,280. Book value on date of sale: $11,520. Sale proceeds: $8,000. Loss on sale = Book Value ($11,520) - Sale Proceeds ($8,000) = $3,520. This loss is debited to the Profit & Loss Account.

questions.question_text: From the following adjustments, prepare the layout adjustments for a Final Accounts problem: Closing stock is $20,000; Outstanding salary is $3,000; Rent received in advance is $1,000; Provide 10% depreciation on Machinery (Book value $40,000); Create Provision for Doubtful Debts at 5% on Debtors (Book value $50,000). Show exactly how these affect the Trading, P&L, and Balance Sheet. [80-100 words]
questions.answer: 1. Closing Stock: Credit Trading A/c $20,000; Show as Current Asset in Balance Sheet $20,000. 2. Outstanding Salary: Add $3,000 to Salary on Debit side of P&L; Show as Current Liability in Balance Sheet. 3. Rent received in advance: Deduct $1,000 from Rent on Credit side of P&L; Show as Current Liability in Balance Sheet. 4. Depreciation: Debit P&L $4,000; Deduct $4,000 from Machinery in Assets. 5. Provision for Doubtful Debts: Debit P&L $2,500; Deduct $2,500 from Debtors in Assets.

questions.question_text: Mr. Y does not keep proper books of accounts. Prepare a Statement of Profit or Loss for the year ending March 31, 2026, and calculate his closing capital. Assets at start: Cash $5,000, Debtors $20,000, Stock $15,000. Liabilities at start: Creditors $10,000. Assets at end: Cash $8,000, Debtors $25,000, Stock $20,000. Liabilities at end: Creditors $12,000. He withdrew $6,000 during the year and introduced $4,000 as additional capital. [80-100 words]
questions.answer: First, calculate Opening Capital = Opening Assets ($40,000) - Opening Liabilities ($10,000) = $30,000. Next, calculate Closing Capital = Closing Assets ($53,000) - Closing Liabilities ($12,000) = $41,000. Prepare the Statement of Profit or Loss: Start with Closing Capital ($41,000). Add Drawings ($6,000) to get $47,000. Less Additional Capital ($4,000) to get Adjusted Closing Capital of $43,000. Less Opening Capital ($30,000). The resulting figure is a Net Profit of $13,000 for the year. His final closing capital before adjustments remains $41,000 in the statement of affairs.
